notes: Golden set for the sim-env-builder skill. 'prompt' is the user's first message (shot 1). 'user_reply' is what the simulated user answers to the confirmation brief (shot 2); it states preferences broadly so it answers whatever the agent asks. 'must_have' and 'checks' are for the judge. tier core = run every iteration; extended = rotated in. v2 (2026-11-10): the simulated user now states the 'checks' success criteria in user_reply, so the judge no longer grades agents on criteria they could not see.

tasks.prompt: I need a simulation environment for self-driving research: a city four-way intersection with traffic lights, a few buildings and trees around it, parked cars along the kerb, and an ego car I can control with steering and throttle. Pedestrians would be nice too.
tasks.user_reply: Looks good. MuJoCo is fine. Keep it to one intersection, two lanes each way. Pedestrians can be simple, walking along the sidewalk or a crosswalk on a fixed path. The ego car should drive through the intersection in the demo. Use your defaults for anything else. Go ahead and build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: ego reaches target speed; ego stays on road; no penetration between cars and road.
must_have: 4-way intersection with 2 lanes each way and lane markings
ego car with steering + throttle actuators
ego car demo drives through the intersection
checks: no penetration between cars and road

tasks.prompt: Build a tabletop manipulation environment: a robot arm with a gripper mounted on a kitchen counter, with a mug, a couple of pieces of fruit and a plate to pick and place. I want a wrist camera and an overhead camera.
tasks.user_reply: Yes, go with MuJoCo and a procedural 6-DoF arm with a parallel gripper. The demo should pick up the mug or a fruit and place it on the plate. Position control of joints is fine. Use defaults for the rest and build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: object lifted > 5 cm by the gripper; objects rest on the counter at start.
must_have: arm with parallel gripper on a counter
pick-and-place demo that actually lifts an object
checks: object lifted > 5 cm by the gripper
objects rest on the counter at start

tasks.prompt: Make me a drone racing environment in a park: a quadcopter, a course of 5 or 6 gates at different heights, trees and some obstacles around. It should be usable for RL.
tasks.user_reply: Great, MuJoCo please. Thrust-per-rotor control is good. Include an onboard FPV camera. The demo should fly through the gates in order. Defaults for everything else; build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: hover holds altitude; passes through gate openings; no collision with gates in the demo.
must_have: demo flies through the gates in order
checks: no collision with gates in the demo

tasks.prompt: I want an environment for training a quadruped robot to walk outdoors: rough hilly terrain, some rocks, a short flight of stairs, and a few trees. The robot should start standing.
tasks.user_reply: MuJoCo is right. A procedural 12-DoF quadruped is fine. The demo only needs to show it standing stably and maybe stepping in place; no need for a real walking policy. Defaults for the rest, go ahead. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: stands 3 s with stable trunk height; feet in contact with terrain; stairs climbable dimensions (rise ~0.15-0.2 m).
must_have: robot spawns on the terrain surface (not inside/above)
checks: stands 3 s with stable trunk height

tasks.prompt: Create a warehouse simulation with pallet racks, pallets with boxes, a forklift parked somewhere, and an autonomous mobile robot that drives between aisles.
tasks.user_reply: Sounds right. MuJoCo. Two or three aisles is enough. The mobile robot can be a differential-drive AMR with a lidar-like sensor or a camera; the demo should drive it down an aisle and stop at a goal. The forklift can be a static prop. Build it with your defaults. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: AMR reaches the goal; AMR does not collide with racks.
must_have: demo drives down an aisle to a goal
checks: AMR does not collide with racks

tasks.prompt: Build a living room environment for a home assistant robot: sofa, coffee table, TV, bookshelf, a rug and some plants. The robot is a mobile base with an arm and should be able to fetch a cup from the coffee table.
tasks.user_reply: Yes. MuJoCo. A wheeled base with a small arm on top is perfect. Demo: drive to the coffee table and reach the cup (grasping is a bonus). Defaults otherwise. Go. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: robot reaches near the table; end effector within 5 cm of the cup.
must_have: demo drives to the table and reaches the cup
checks: end effector within 5 cm of the cup

tasks.prompt: I need a Mars exploration environment: a rover driving over cratered rocky terrain with Mars gravity, a lander module in the distance, and some boulders.
tasks.user_reply: MuJoCo, yes. A simple 4- or 6-wheel rover with skid or Ackermann steering is fine; give it a mast camera. Demo: drive the rover across the terrain toward the lander. Use reddish terrain. Defaults otherwise; build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: gravity probe matches 3.71; rover stays upright; rover makes progress.

tasks.prompt: Make a harbor environment with a small boat on the water, a wooden dock, a few buoys and a lighthouse. The boat needs to float and be controllable with a thruster and rudder.
tasks.user_reply: MuJoCo please. Approximate buoyancy is fine. Demo: the boat motors out around a buoy. Defaults otherwise, build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: boat floats at a stable waterline; boat does not sink or fly; thrust moves the boat.
checks: boat floats at a stable waterline
boat does not sink or fly

tasks.prompt: Agricultural scene: an apple orchard with rows of trees, a tractor parked at the end of a row, a barn, and a small ground robot that drives between the tree rows for inspection.
tasks.user_reply: Yes, MuJoCo. Four rows of trees is enough. The ground robot can be a small wheeled rover with a camera; demo drives down one row. Defaults otherwise. Go ahead. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: robot stays between rows; robot reaches the end of the row.
checks: robot reaches the end of the row

tasks.prompt: Create a robot soccer environment: a small field with goals, a ball, and two teams of two wheeled robots each, for multi-agent RL.
tasks.user_reply: MuJoCo is good. Differential-drive robots are fine. Demo: one robot pushes the ball toward a goal. The env should expose all four robots' actions and observations. Defaults otherwise; build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: ball rolls with realistic friction; robot can push the ball.
must_have: 4 wheeled robots in two team colours
demo pushes the ball toward a goal

tasks.prompt: We want photorealistic synthetic camera data of a retail store aisle (shelves with products, shopping carts, price signs) for training a detector, and we will run thousands of randomized variations on our RTX 4090 workstation with Isaac. Can you build the environment?
tasks.user_reply: Our RTX machine is separate from this laptop. Please build and test it locally in MuJoCo and also export the Isaac Sim USD stage plus a script I can run there. Add a camera that looks down the aisle. Defaults for the rest. Go ahead. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: USD validation passes; MuJoCo smoke passes.
tasks.expected_backend: isaac (via MuJoCo build + USD export, since no RTX GPU here)
must_have: recognises Isaac fits but cannot run here and says so
honest statement that Isaac runtime was not executed

tasks.prompt: Just a classic cart-pole environment please, nothing fancy, for quick RL experiments.
tasks.user_reply: Yes, MuJoCo, standard dimensions, force-controlled cart, Gym API. Keep it minimal. Build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: pole falls without control; a simple LQR/PD controller balances it.
must_have: cart on a rail (slide joint with limits)
Gym-style env with reward for keeping the pole up
checks: a simple LQR/PD controller balances it

tasks.prompt: Industrial cell: a conveyor belt carrying boxes of different colours, a robot arm next to it that sorts them into bins, safety fences around the cell.
tasks.user_reply: MuJoCo. The conveyor can move boxes by setting their velocity, no need for a real belt. Demo: the arm picks at least one box off the conveyor and drops it in the matching bin. Defaults otherwise, build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: boxes travel along the conveyor; a box ends up inside a bin.
must_have: demo sorts at least one box into a bin
checks: a box ends up inside a bin

tasks.prompt: A biology lab bench environment for a lab automation robot: a centrifuge, a pipette rack, test tube racks with tubes, a microscope, and a small robot arm that moves a test tube from one rack to another.
tasks.user_reply: MuJoCo, procedural arm is fine. If some lab equipment is not available as a model, generate it. Demo: move one test tube between racks. Defaults otherwise; go. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: tube is grasped and moved; tubes stand upright in racks at start.
must_have: procedural fallbacks for missing equipment that still look recognisable
checks: tubes stand upright in racks at start

tasks.prompt: I need a deformable-object environment: a square cloth lying on a table that a robot arm could fold, for research on cloth manipulation.
tasks.user_reply: MuJoCo with its flex/cloth support. Demo: the arm grabs one corner of the cloth and lifts it (folding is a bonus). Defaults otherwise, build it. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: cloth is stable for 3 s; cloth corner rises when lifted.
must_have: cloth rests on the table without exploding

tasks.prompt: Set up an environment for training a humanoid robot to walk: a flat floor with some low obstacles and a ramp, inside a simple gym hall.
tasks.user_reply: MuJoCo. A procedural humanoid in the style of the classic MuJoCo humanoid (torque or position actuators) is fine; no real robot download. The demo just needs to show it standing with a PD hold or collapsing physically plausibly. Defaults; go. Please make sure these hold, with a check for each: joint limits respected; no self-penetration explosion.
must_have: demo shows standing hold or plausible fall
